evidence.observation: Resolves metadata for a model as an exact key lookup: first the locally registered model metadata (self.local_model_metadata, populated from a --model-metadata-file via register_litellm_models), then the cached litellm price/context DB. When the name matches nothing it returns dict() rather than inventing context-window, cost or provider values, so an unknown model is represented explicitly as 'no metadata'.

Fallback chain for model facts: cached DB lookup, then litellm.get_model_info (which raises for unmapped models and is caught), then OpenRouter scraping only for openrouter/-prefixed names. For an unrecognized non-openrouter model the function returns the empty cached_info, i.e. an explicit empty result, never synthesized capabilities such as max_input_tokens or supports_* flags.

Constructs a model by aliasing the name, storing self.info from get_model_info(model), validating the environment, then deriving max_chat_history_tokens from info.get('max_input_tokens') with a documented 1k-8k clamp. An empty info (unknown model) therefore yields the documented sane defaults instead of a silently assumed large context window.

Declares the per-model settings dataclass, including accepts_settings (default None) - the sole list of optional capabilities aider may request (e.g. thinking_tokens, reasoning_effort). Capability support is opt-in data here or appended by name heuristics; it is never inferred from a model merely being constructible, so an unknown model starts with no claimed capabilities.

Applies capability settings only when the lowercased model name matches a built-in heuristic (o1/o3-mini, gpt-4.1/gpt-5, deepseek r1/v3, llama3-70b, qwen/qwq, sonnet-4/opus-4, etc.), appending to accepts_settings only inside those branches. An unmatched unknown model falls through to the defaults with accepts_settings left empty, so it cannot silently claim unsupported capabilities like reasoning_effort or thinking_tokens.

Loads a local model metadata fixture (JSON5 file, e.g. .prale-eval/fixtures/local-model-metadata.json) and merges it into model_info_manager.local_model_metadata with exact per-name granularity via dict.update. Registration is therefore explicit and bounded: only the declared model names become known, and no sibling or provider-wide names are implied.

Emits explicit user-facing warnings for models that are not fully known: missing/unknown environment keys, and - when model.info is empty - 'Warning for <model>: Unknown context window size and costs, using sane defaults.' followed by fuzzy 'Did you mean' suggestions. It returns show=True in that case, so unknown-model handling is surfaced rather than silent.

Builds the set of known chat models from litellm.model_cost plus the locally registered metadata, then looks for substring or difflib close matches. A model name with no real counterpart returns an empty list, so an unknown name is never echoed back as if it were a recognized model.

claims.claim: Unknown-model handling in aider.models is explicit for metadata: a model that is neither registered from a local metadata fixture nor known to litellm resolves to an empty dict ({}) from both ModelInfoManager.get_model_from_cached_json_db and ModelInfoManager.get_model_info, so no context-window, cost or provider values are fabricated.

An unknown model receives the documented sane defaults rather than an assumed capability profile: Model.__init__ stores the empty info and clamps max_chat_history_tokens to the 1k-8k range, while apply_generic_model_settings only appends to accepts_settings inside recognized name-heuristic branches, leaving accepts_settings empty for an unmatched model.

The absence of capability claims is observable and non-vacuous: sanity_check_model emits the explicit warning 'Unknown context window size and costs, using sane defaults.' and returns True for an unknown model, while a model whose name is known to support reasoning (gpt-5.5) does list reasoning_effort in accepts_settings, demonstrating the check distinguishes the two cases.

Registration of a local model metadata fixture is exact and bounded: register_litellm_models merges the fixture into model_info_manager.local_model_metadata by name, so only declared models gain metadata and an unregistered sibling name remains unknown (returns {}); fuzzy_match_models likewise never returns an unknown name as a recognized model.

conclusion: The aider contract holds: given a distinct local model metadata fixture registered through register_litellm_models, a fixture-declared model resolves to exactly the fixture's facts, while a model unknown everywhere is handled explicitly - empty metadata from get_model_from_cached_json_db/get_model_info, the documented sane defaults in Model.__init__, an explicit 'Unknown context window size and costs' warning from sanity_check_model, and an empty accepts_settings list so no unsupported capability (thinking_tokens, reasoning_effort) is silently claimed. The executable demo .prale-eval/demo_unknown_model_contract.py verifies all nine clauses (9/9 passed, exit 0).

validation.notes: 9/9 contract checks passed with exit status 0. The demo registers .prale-eval/fixtures/local-model-metadata.json via register_litellm_models and drives the real aider.models code paths (ModelInfoManager.get_model_from_cached_json_db, get_model_info, Model.__init__, apply_generic_model_settings, sanity_check_model, fuzzy_match_models). Limitation: litellm, json5 and oslex are not installed in this environment and no dependencies may be installed; the demo installs minimal in-process stand-ins for exactly those three imports, so all aider logic under test is the repository's real code and only the absent third-party provider client is substituted. The run is hermetic (HOME redirected to a workspace temp dir, model_info_manager cache hooks neutralised) and no files outside the workspace were read or written.
